:::{#thm-countable-implies-finite}
#### Countable additivity implies finite additivity

If $\measure$ is a [countably additive](#def-countable-additivity) function
on a [$\sigma$-algebra](#def-sigma-algebra) $\salg$,
and $\measure(\emptyset) = 0$,
then $\measure$ is [finitely additive](#def-finite-additivity).

:::

::: proof

Let $\dsn{A}$ be pairwise disjoint sets in $\salg$,
and extend them to a sequence by setting $A_{n+1} = A_{n+2} = \cdots = \emptyset$.
The extended sequence is still pairwise disjoint,
since $\emptyset$ shares no element with any set,
and its union is $A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n$. So:

$$
\ba
\measure(A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n)
&= \measure\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right)
&& \text{(} A_i = \emptyset \text{ for } i > n \text{)} \\
&= \sumto{i}{\infty} \measure(A_i)
&& \text{(countable additivity)} \\
&= \sumin \measure(A_i) + \sum_{i=n+1}^{\infty} \measure(\emptyset)
&& \text{(} A_i = \emptyset \text{ for } i > n \text{)} \\
&= \sumin \measure(A_i)
&& \text{(} \measure(\emptyset) = 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
